parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Two random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the independent distributions $\text{N}(7, 3)$ and $\text{N}(6, 2)$ respectively. A random value of each variable is taken.

Find the probability that the two values differ by more than 2.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Each candidate’s overall score in a science test is calculated as follows. The mark for theory is denoted by $T$, the mark for practical is denoted by $P$, and the overall score is given by $T + 1.5P$. The variables $T$ and $P$ are assumed to be independent with distributions $\text{N}(62, 158)$ and $\text{N}(42, 108)$ respectively. You should assume that no continuity corrections are needed when using these distributions.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
A pass is awarded to candidates whose overall score is at least 90.

Find the proportion of candidates who pass.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Comment on the assumption that the variables $T$ and $P$ are independent.
